newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDEN'S ASBRINK SAYS FINANCIAL SYSTEMS KEY.
newsitem.headline: SWEDEN'S ASBRINK SAYS FINANCIAL SYSTEMS KEY.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Wednesday that healthy financial systems were vital for the continued progress of the Baltic states in their aim to become fully market-oriented nations.

Asbrink, the key note speaker at a Euromoney conference on the Baltic capital markets here, said Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia have responded well to the economic changes after regaining independence from the former Soviet Union.
"Promoting robust financial systems in economies in transition is of vital importance," Asbrink said.
"The success of other reforms depends on the health of the financial sector. The Baltic countries responded postively to global changes in the financial system and economies," he added.
He downplayed the significance of the countries various banking crises and said one of the root causes was under-capitalisation.
"The direct costs and indirect costs of the crisis appear to have been limited," he added.
"The conditions are there for continued positive trends," Asbrink said.
